messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: EIGEN_INITIALIZE_MATRICES_BY_ZERO on?
parts:
Hi!

As we had a bit of trouble with Eigen not initializing correctly, as I recall, should we consider to switch on the macro

EIGEN_INITIALIZE_MATRICES_BY_ZERO

? I have seen by now a number of issues which may have been avoided by the above, I guess.

Taken from: http://eigen.tuxfamily.org/dox/TopicPreprocessorDirectives.html

Best,

Sebastian

messages.author: 6db62e08ec862130
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] EIGEN_INITIALIZE_MATRICES_BY_ZERO on?
parts:
On Wed, Oct 14, 2015 at 05:21:16AM -0700, Sebastian Weber wrote:
> As we had a bit of trouble with Eigen not initializing correctly, as
> I recall, should we consider to switch on the macro
>
> EIGEN_INITIALIZE_MATRICES_BY_ZERO
>
> ? I have seen by now a number of issues which may have been avoided
> by the above, I guess.

Initializing matrices actually takes time. If you start down the road
of initializing with zero then it is difficult to go back.

In OpenMx, we use EIGEN_INITIALIZE_MATRICES_BY_NAN when to catch bugs
when running tests and then turn it off for normal compiles.

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] EIGEN_INITIALIZE_MATRICES_BY_ZERO on?
parts:
I agree that enabling this for testing runs only makes sense. Initializing stuff should be up to the user who anyway thinks of initialization in some way (or doesn't do it on purpose as things get overwritten).

So how about enabling it for testing runs? Either the set 0 or the set NA - whatever makes more sense (I am not sure).

Sebastian
